context.clinical_context_summary: 56-year-old male with extensive past medical history including severe neurological injury (intracranial injury with prolonged LOC, paraplegia, hydrocephalus, seizure disorder), chronic respiratory compromise (bronchiectasis, pulmonary mycobacterial infection, history of aspiration pneumonitis, acute respiratory failure with hypoxia), and prior sepsis/septic shock. Currently has tracheostomy and gastrostomy status, indicating chronic ventilatory support needs. On albuterol for bronchodilation, aspirin for cardiovascular protection, and amantadine. Presents with SHORTNESS OF BREATH - HIGH RISK given history of respiratory failure, aspiration risk, and chronic lung disease. IMMUNOCOMPROMISED RISK due to debility and recurrent infections. Temperature data suggests oral/core measurement (mean 37.12°C, range 36.7-38.3°C). Baseline SpO2 shows episodes of desaturation (lowest 89.1%) consistent with chronic respiratory disease.
context.rationale: Thresholds personalized for a complex neurologically impaired patient with chronic respiratory disease and history of sepsis. HR range accounts for baseline tachycardia tendency (mean 87 bpm) while remaining conservative. BP thresholds widened slightly as baseline SBP runs low (mean 88 mmHg) - likely related to autonomic dysfunction from spinal cord injury (paraplegia); however critical hypotension threshold kept at 75 mmHg given sepsis history. SpO2 normal floor set at 90% acknowledging chronic lung disease and bronchiectasis, but warning at 88% given acute presentation with dyspnea. RR normal ceiling set at 24 brpm (his current mean) as chronic respiratory patients often have elevated baseline; warning at 28 brpm signals acute distress. Temperature thresholds lowered for fever detection (37.8°C/38.5°C) given immunocompromised status from debility and need for early sepsis recognition in this high-risk patient.
